name: The Ledger Knife
description: A short blade whose spine is scored with a tally nobody finished.
benefit: Strikes against anyone who owes a debt, a due or a favour land hard and bypass guard.
cost: Drawn inside a settlement it costs standing with that polis, which reads it as a collector's threat.

name: The Eleventh Spear
description: Ten spears were offered at the altar. This one was kept back.
benefit: Long reach, and each kill returns a measure of the vitality it cost.
cost: Every thrust draws a little vitality from the wielder first; at low vitality it will not lift.

name: Xiphos Sworn on the Styx
description: The edge was quenched in water that binds even gods, and it remembers who held the cup.
benefit: Never needs repair and never dulls.
cost: Each fight adds to a debt that is called in when the next oath is sworn.

name: Mace of the Bronze Assize
description: A judge's staff, cast solid so that no sentence is argued with twice.
benefit: Breaks a foe's poise in one blow and ends their guard.
cost: Slow to recover after a swing, and heavy enough to drain stamina just by being carried at a run.

name: The Salt Hook
description: Fishermen of the drowned quarter used it on things that were not fish.
benefit: Hauls a foe off a ledge, out of a boat or down from a wall.
cost: Brine eats it; repairs cost twice as much and it fails in the dry as often as the wet.

name: Horn Bow of the Cretan Watch
description: Strung with sinew from a herd that no longer exists.
benefit: Strikes from beyond the range any garrison expects to be threatened.
cost: The string sings when drawn, and every watcher within earshot is told where you are.

name: Reaper's Sickle of Mount Ash
description: The blade warms in the hand the way a stone does after a day in the sun.
benefit: Each strike also strips a charge's worth of power from whatever it cuts.
cost: It feeds on the charges the wielder carries too, and will empty a full pouch over a long week.

name: The Blind Seer's Cane
description: Ash wood, worn smooth. It taps twice before every danger.
benefit: Warns of an ambush or a trap a few steps before it springs.
cost: A poor weapon: it deals almost nothing, and it fills the weapon slot so no real blade can be carried beside it.

name: Kerameikos Cleaver
description: A butcher's blade from the cemetery district, kept for the work no one admits to.
benefit: Cuts through the risen dead cleanly and leaves them down.
cost: The unburied remember it; they find the wielder first and in greater number.

name: Flail of Spilled Wine
description: Two jars on a chain, sealed with pitch. One is always a little heavier than the other.
benefit: Strikes round a raised guard and staggers a shielded foe.
cost: Wild and slow to recover; a miss opens the wielder to the first reply.

name: Hoplon of the Last Rank
description: The shield of the man who stood where the line broke, and did not move.
benefit: Blocks nearly anything from the front and takes the full force of a blow without staggering.
cost: Too heavy to run or climb with; the wielder walks, or sets it down.

name: Aegis of the Silent Oracle
description: Goatskin over bronze, with a face painted on it that has been scraped out.
benefit: A raised guard parries for longer than any other shield and breaks the attacker's poise.
cost: It covers little. A blow that gets past the parry lands in full.

name: Pelte of the Eastern Riders
description: A crescent of wicker and hide, light as a hat.
benefit: Barely slows the wielder, and a quick parry opens a riposte.
cost: It splinters on a heavy blow and has to be rebuilt in a settlement.

name: Helm of Hades
description: A plain bronze helmet that nobody can describe afterwards.
benefit: Sentries notice the wielder at a third of the usual distance.
cost: The wearer's own sight narrows to a slit, and allies in the dark lose track of them too.

name: Laurel of the Purified
description: A wreath cut by hand at a spring, replaced each dawn by someone who is not named.
benefit: Wards off the slow sickness of the Miasma while worn.
cost: It withers with every kill and must be re-cut at a sanctuary, so the wearer cannot fight and stay clean.

name: Diver's Bell Helm
description: An inverted copper bell with a leather skirt. A pocket of air goes down with you.
benefit: Lets the wearer go under the surface for as long as the bell holds air.
cost: Dead weight on land and a poor fit with any other helmet; it must be stowed or carried.

name: Cork Cuirass
description: Sailors wore it over the side when the deck went. Most of them are still wearing it.
benefit: Keeps the wearer afloat and moving across deep water.
cost: It stops arrows but not blades, and tears on the first heavy hit, leaving the wearer to swim unaided.

name: Contractor's Linothorax
description: Glued linen, stamped with a mark that means this one is already paid for.
benefit: Strong cover, and League posts treat the wearer as a signed party and do not search them.
cost: Every non-League faction reads the stamp as a side taken and charges accordingly.

name: Mantle of the Ash Mnemones
description: Grey wool that never quite stops smelling of a fire.
benefit: Fire, brine and blight do the wearer no harm.
cost: It offers no cover against steel, and burns the wearer's hands if the charge pouch is open.

name: Shroud of the Kept Dead
description: A burial cloth, unused. The family who bought it never arrived.
benefit: The risen dead take the wearer for one of their own and pass by.
cost: The living find it grim: merchants will not haggle and guards ask questions.

name: Shepherd's Spurs
description: Iron claws strapped to the instep, forged for herds that crossed the high scree.
benefit: Lets the wearer scale faces that have holds, and sets a firm footing on ice.
cost: Loud on stone and deadly on a wooden floor; the wearer cannot move quietly with them on.

name: Sandals of the Marathon Courier
description: Thin soles, worn through twice and mended each time by someone fond of him.
benefit: A long run costs very little stamina.
cost: They hold no armour and make every landing a danger; a fall from any real height maims.

name: Smith's Gauntlets
description: Blackened with a hundred years of other people's mistakes.
benefit: Repairs cost half as much, and the wearer can mend a weapon in the field.
cost: Clumsy for fine work: locks stay shut and bowstrings slip.

name: Pearl Diver's Bladder
description: A pig's bladder on a cord, lined with wax and breathed from twice.
benefit: Doubles the time the wearer can stay underwater unaided.
cost: It bursts under a heavy blow, and a spare takes a full season in a settlement to prepare.

name: Splinter of the Pythia's Tripod
description: Whatever sat on it once spoke. The splinter still hums when it is quiet.
benefit: Reveals a hint of the Pressure's next step in a dream each night.
cost: The dream costs sleep; the wearer wakes without rest and stamina recovers slower the more they see.

name: The Last Favour Ring
description: A plain band engraved with a number. The number goes down.
benefit: Doubles the power of every spent charge.
cost: A fixed number of uses remain, and when it reaches zero the ring is gone with the favour.

name: Initiate's Wax Seal
description: A signet pressed into a lump of red wax that has never fully set.
benefit: Opens any door that a rite of the cult has reached, without a bribe.
cost: Revealed to a rival cult, it cancels the wearer's admission and the seal runs to blood.

name: The Debt Bell
description: A little bell that rings once for every obligation the carrier owes.
benefit: Lets the carrier settle a payment in an obligation owed by someone else.
cost: It rings aloud when the carrier is in debt, and a creditor within hearing will know.

name: Hemp Cable of Daidalos
description: Forty fathoms of tarred hemp, knotted by someone who built a maze and knew how to leave one.
benefit: Lets the wearer rope down a drop and back up it, without damage.
cost: Nine kilograms to carry, and the rope itself must be left behind on a one-way descent.

name: Charon's Spare Oar
description: Oak, black with handling. It does not belong to any boat, and any boat will accept it.
benefit: Lets the carrier take a small boat across open water, however still.
cost: Each crossing demands a coin at the far shore, set into the oar's blade and never returned.
